Battery optimisation, the Restricted choice, the permission reset and Battery Saver are all read from Android itself, so their states above are real. Restricted stops every background run outright; the permission reset takes the photos permission away from an app that is not opened for a few months, which is exactly what a set-and-forget app is; Battery Saver pauses runs until it is turned off, which most phones do by themselves while charging. Auto-launch and background activity are the phone maker\u2019s own switches. Android gives apps no way to read them, which is why they cannot say On or Off \u2014 and on Realme, Oppo, Xiaomi and Vivo phones, one of them being off is the usual reason work stops a day after setup. Two more of the maker\u2019s modes cannot be read either and do the same: Super power saving (or Ultra battery saver) ends every background app while it is on, and Realme\u2019s Sleep standby optimisation freezes apps overnight \u2014 both are under Settings › Battery. If the phone keeps stopping the work, Ente Saver says so in a notification at most once a week and three times in all, then leaves it to the chip on Home. Waiting on purpose \u2014 for Battery Saver, or for the charger in charging-only mode \u2014 never counts as being stopped.

Ente Saver never uploads anything: it holds no internet permission, so there is no code in it that could. It only makes a smaller copy of each photo and video and puts it in one folder. Ente Photos uploads that folder. Two apps, one job each \u2014 and because the upload is Ente\'s own, your files reach Ente with its own encryption, in your own account.
Private, and kept exactly as sent

Ente Photos is end-to-end encrypted, open source and independently audited, so only you can see your photos. It stores what it is given without shrinking it again, so the saving Ente Saver made is the saving you keep. The free plan holds 10 GB, and optimised copies make it go much further.

In Ente, open Settings \u203a Backup \u203a Backed up folders. Turn on the Ente Saver folder (or folders) and turn off Camera. Backing up both stores every photo twice \u2014 once full size, once optimised \u2014 and fills your plan faster than using no Ente Saver at all. This is the most expensive mistake available here, which is why setup shows it before anything runs.

Your whole library sits in one Ente account: one 24-word recovery key, one timeline. Ente\'s face recognition and magic search run on your phone, and they work on the copies too once machine learning is turned on in Ente (Settings \u203a Machine learning).
How Ente Saver knows a copy arrived

When you use Free up device space in Ente (Settings \u203a Free up space \u203a Free up device space), Ente removes the files it has already uploaded, including the copies in the Ente Saver folder. A copy disappearing that way is the proof. With Usage access on, Ente Saver can also measure how much Ente sent while a copy was waiting. Even with proof, an original is offered for removal only after a 30-day safety wait.
If Ente is not installed yet

Everything still runs. Photos are optimised on the usual schedule and the copies wait in the folder, using the space you allowed. Once that space is full, Ente Saver stops making more and says so on Home. Nothing can be freed until Ente has the copies. Install Ente Photos from the Play Store, F-Droid or ente.com \u2014 Settings has the buttons \u2014 and the waiting copies go up on its next backup, with nothing redone.
If you used another cloud app before

Copies already uploaded there stay in that account, and Ente Saver never sends them again. From version 11, Ente Saver works with Ente Photos only. Nothing on this phone was deleted by the change, and your originals are where they were. If the other app still backs up the folder, you can turn that off in it.
Ente can be the place you look at your photos, not only where they are kept. One app, and no wondering which one to open.

Set Ente as the default gallery, so a photo you tap in another app opens in Ente. It is in Android Settings \u203a Apps \u203a Default apps, and the button below opens it. If your phone lists no gallery there, choose Ente and Always the next time Android asks which app should open a photo.
Ente can change its own icon. In Ente, open Settings \u203a General \u203a Advanced \u203a App icon and pick one of several looks.

Ente Saver includes one icon, made for Ente alone: a cloud holding a photo and a video, with Ente\'s green heart on it, in Ente Photos\' own style, the same one the shortcut below uses. On Realme, Oppo and OnePlus phones, long-press Ente Photos on the home screen \u203a Edit, tap its icon and pick it under Ente Saver icons. Nova, Lawnchair and other launchers have their own icon pack or edit-icon setting. With Ente from the Play Store, applying the pack changes Ente\'s icon and no other app\'s; with Ente from F-Droid or ente.com, pick it for Ente in the launcher\'s edit-icon screen. A launcher\'s edit screen may also offer it when you edit some other app; that list is the launcher\'s, so just pick it for Ente. Keep Ente\'s own app icon on its green look, so every launcher finds it. The launcher may take a moment to update. The icon lives inside Ente Saver: uninstall it, and Ente gets its own icon back.

Add a shortcut to your home screen that opens Ente, with a Photos icon and the name you pick: Photos, Gallery, Cloud Photos, or your own name of up to 12 letters. Some launchers show a small badge on shortcuts. Uninstalling Ente Saver removes the shortcut too; Ente and your photos stay.
Some launchers let you rename an app: long-press its icon \u203a Edit. Not every phone has this.
Turn on machine learning in Ente (Settings \u203a Machine learning) for face recognition and magic search. It runs on the phone itself, and it works on Ente Saver\'s copies too.
Ente\'s Free up device space also removes Ente Saver\'s copies once they are uploaded. That is expected \u2014 it is exactly how Ente Saver knows they arrived.
Two apps do the job: Ente Saver makes the smaller copies and puts them in one folder; Ente Photos uploads that folder. Ente Saver never uploads anything and never deletes an original on its own.

Ente Saver will still optimise your photos and videos on its usual schedule, and the smaller copies will wait in the Ente Saver folder. Nothing is uploaded until you install Ente Photos and back up that folder in it. Until then the copies use the space you allowed, and no original can be offered for removal. You can finish setup now and install Ente Photos whenever you like.
Ente and Ente Photos belong to their owner and are named here only to say which app Ente Saver works with. Ente Saver is independent, and is not made by or connected with Ente.

Every official build is published at github.com/smmpanelusertestai07-dotcom/EnteSaver, with its checksum. Something wrong? Report it there; the page opens in your browser, Ente Saver itself never goes online.
What the app stores, and what it never does.

Ente Photos keeps your photos private with end-to-end encryption, and it stores exactly what you hand it — it does not make a file smaller first. So a library of 4K video fills a plan quickly, and the only answer usually on offer is to buy more storage every year.

Ente Saver is the step in between. It optimises your photos and videos on the phone itself, into one folder Ente backs up, so the same library reaches Ente in a fraction of the space — the free 10 GB or a small plan goes a great deal further.

It looks after the phone as well as the plan: it saves the heavy work for when the phone is charging, cool and idle, keeps the free space you asked it to keep, finds duplicate files and your largest ones, and never removes an original unless you confirm it yourself.
Works entirely on your phone. No account, no ads, and no internet permission at all.

resources.string: %1$d no longer qualified and were left alone (%2$s).

It makes a smaller copy of each photo and video in the albums you chose, and puts those copies in one folder on your phone. Ente Photos backs up that folder, end-to-end encrypted, so only the small copies are uploaded and your Ente storage lasts much longer. Your originals stay exactly where they are, untouched. Everything happens on the phone: Ente Saver has no internet permission and cannot upload anything itself.
Where do the optimised copies go, and what do I select in Ente Photos?

They go to the Ente Saver folder. In Settings you can give it your own name, or use separate folders for photos and videos, and the Storage screen prints the exact path with a copy button. After an upgrade from an earlier version, copies keep going to the old Pictures/CloudSaver folder until you tap Move on Home. In Ente Photos, open Settings \u203a Backup \u203a Backed up folders and turn that folder on \u2014 and turn off Camera, or you will be uploading the big originals as well. The folder also appears as an album in your gallery while files wait to be collected \u2014 that is what lets Ente see it. Most gallery apps can hide an album from their own settings. Ente Saver never hides it itself, because that would hide it from Ente too. One more thing: anything you put into the folder yourself is left exactly where it is \u2014 Ente Saver never moves, renames or removes a file it did not create \u2014 but Ente Photos will upload it at full size, so Home shows a note whenever that happens.

No. Ente Saver never edits, moves or deletes an original by itself, at any point, for any reason. The only way an original is ever removed is if you open Free up space, select files yourself, and confirm Android\'s own deletion dialog. On Android 11 and newer it goes to your gallery trash first, where it stays about 30 days; on Android 10 there is no media trash, so Android removes it straight away and says so in its own dialog.

On the default setting, a 12-megapixel photo comes out about 30% smaller with no difference you can see on a phone. Photos above 16 megapixels come down to 16, saving about 75%. Video is capped at 1080p and comes out 60\u201375% smaller, keeping close to the original at normal viewing size. Higher and lower settings are in Settings under Quality, and the app shows what it actually measured on your own files.
Are dates, locations and file names kept?

Yes. Every copy carries the original\'s shooting date and camera details, and the file date is set to match. The GPS location comes too, as long as you allowed the location request during setup \u2014 Android hands apps a copy with the location removed unless that one is granted. Everything else is carried either way. That is why the copies land in the right place chronologically in Ente instead of all appearing as today. The file name keeps the original name with a short code added, so a copy can always be matched back to its original.
How does Ente Saver know a file reached Ente?

Two ways, both watched automatically. When you use Free up device space in Ente (Settings \u203a Free up space \u203a Free up device space), Ente removes the copies it has already uploaded from the folder; a copy that disappears without Ente Saver removing it is the proof. Ente Saver also adds copies a few at a time, and with Usage access on it watches how much data Ente Photos sends, so a matching amount right after one file goes out counts for that file. That weaker proof is used in Free up space only if you turn it on in Settings. Every file shows which of the two applies to it, in plain words, and files with no proof are never offered for removal. Even with proof, an original is offered only after a 30-day safety wait. The daily limit in Settings controls how much Ente Saver adds to the upload folder each day \u2014 which is what Ente Photos then uploads. Ente Saver cannot control when Ente uploads or which network it uses; set that inside Ente Photos.
How do I make Ente work like my phone\'s gallery?

Set Ente as the default gallery in Android Settings \u203a Apps \u203a Default apps, so photos you open from other apps show in Ente. Give it a gallery-style icon, either with Ente\'s own setting (Ente \u203a Settings \u203a General \u203a Advanced \u203a App icon) or with Ente Saver\'s icon pack in a launcher that supports icon packs. Or, from Help \u203a Make Ente your gallery, add a Photos shortcut to your home screen that opens Ente. Then turn on machine learning in Ente for face recognition and magic search. That help page walks through each step.
Someone deleted a file from the Ente Saver folder \u2014 what now?

If Ente Saver had already confirmed that file reached Ente, nothing happens: the disappearance is exactly what an upload looks like, and the original was never at risk. If it had not been confirmed, Ente Saver treats the copy as lost and simply makes it again on the next run. Either way your original is untouched, because the app only ever removes an original after you confirm it yourself.
What about HEIC, RAW, GIF and motion photos?

A HEIC photo is optimised like any other. Copies are written as HEIC, JPEG or WebP: on Auto, HEIC only where this phone\'s chip passes a quick check, and JPEG otherwise. RAW, GIF and similar formats are copied exactly as they are, because optimising them either loses something that matters or makes the file bigger. Motion photos and depth photos are copied whole, so their moving or depth part stays intact, and Ultra HDR photos stay JPEG so they keep their HDR. Anything copied unchanged is listed on the Files screen so you can see it happened on purpose \u2014 it is the app refusing to damage something, not a failure.
What happens if I uninstall, clear data, or change phones?

Your photos are unaffected. Optimised copies stay in the Ente Saver folder until Ente Photos collects them, kept light copies stay in your gallery, and your Ente account is untouched. When you uninstall, Android asks whether to keep the app\'s data: keep it, and a reinstall carries on as before. Otherwise Ente Saver\'s history is saved every day as history.json in Documents \u203a Ente Saver. After a reinstall, or on a new phone with that file copied across, tap Restore from a backup file on the first screen and choose it, so nothing is optimised or sent twice.
What does freeing up space do, and can I get files back?

It is the one screen that can remove an original, and it only ever removes what you select. It lists files whose copies Ente has provably collected, shows the proof for each one, and offers three modes \u2014 keep a light copy in your gallery, remove the original entirely, or just clear the copies waiting on your phone. Unless you pick Delete permanently, removed files go to your gallery trash, where Android keeps them for 30 days, and the Recently freed up screen lists every batch with a Restore button. Delete permanently skips the trash and cannot be undone. Android 10 has no gallery trash, so there every removal is final and is asked for one file at a time. If you choose the light-copy mode, the copies live in the Pictures/Light copies album \u2014 keep that album out of Ente\'s backed up folders, because every file there already reached Ente once and backing the album up would store it twice.

Nothing, from Ente Saver. The internet permission is removed from the app itself, so there is no code path that could send anything anywhere \u2014 not analytics, not crash reports, not your photos. All the network traffic you will see is Ente Photos uploading the folder, end-to-end encrypted, exactly as it would for any other folder. You can check this yourself in Android\'s app info screen, where Ente Saver has no network permission to grant or deny.
Why is there an Optimise now button if everything is automatic?

The schedule waits for good moments \u2014 charging, screen off, the day\u2019s allowance. The button skips the waiting, never the safety limits: it will not run when the phone is too hot, the battery is under 15%, or free space is below the reserve. The run is listed in Activity as \u201cStarted by you\u201d.
What is the Ente Saver folder in Documents?

It holds one small text file, history.json: a list of file names, dates, sizes and short codes \u2014 never photos. It is rewritten every day, and it is what lets a reinstall or a new phone pick up where you left off: tap Restore from a backup file on the first screen and choose it. Deleting it is safe; the app writes it again within a day. Older versions kept this list in folders called .cloudsaver or _.cloudsaver; any left over can be deleted. The Backup and restore buttons in Settings make an extra copy you keep somewhere else, like a computer.
Where do the “Recommended for this phone” figures come from?

From this phone, measured on the spot: how much storage it has in total, and how much of it is free right now. A 64 GB phone and a 512 GB phone should not hold back the same headroom, so the app works out a reserve of about a twentieth of the phone (never under 1.5 GB), a daily limit that drops to the cautious figure on a small or nearly full phone, and a ceiling on its own working space of about a tenth of what is free, capped at 5 GB and never so low that the pipeline jams against it. Nothing is measured off the phone and no usage is sent anywhere. It is only ever an offer: the figure sits under the setting with a Use recommended button, your own value is never overwritten, and the line turns into a warning only when what is stored has drifted more than three times away from it.
Can the smaller copy stay in the same album instead of a new folder?

Yes. In Free up space, choose “Replace with light copy” and turn on “Keep it in the same album”. The optimised copy is then written into the album the original was in, under the original’s name and carrying its date, camera details and location — so your gallery timeline does not move and no extra folder appears. The copy is written and checked first; only then does Android ask you to confirm removing the original, and refusing leaves both untouched. Two honest caveats: the copy keeps the format it was optimised to, so a HEIC photo can come back as .jpg, and the file now in your album is the optimised version rather than the byte-for-byte original. Ente Saver recognises the replacement as the same photo, so it is never optimised a second time.
Why only Ente Photos, and what if it isn\'t installed?

Ente Photos is end-to-end encrypted and keeps every file exactly as it was sent, so the space Ente Saver saved is the space you keep. When it frees up device space it removes its own uploads from the folder, which is how Ente Saver proves a copy arrived. It checks duplicates by content, so a file sent twice is stored once. And if Ente downloads a copy back to your phone \u2014 into Download or any album \u2014 Ente Saver recognises its own copies by their names and never optimises or re-sends them. You also get one recovery key and one timeline, with Ente\'s on-device face recognition and magic search. If Ente Photos is not installed yet, copies are still made and wait in the folder, using the space you allowed. Nothing is ever freed until Ente has them. Install it from the Play Store, F-Droid or ente.com, turn on the Ente Saver folder in it, and the waiting copies go up on its next backup.
Why does the Files list look empty when Free up space still finds things?

They answer different questions. Files is the work list: it shows what Ente Saver is going to optimise and what it already has, so it only ever covers the albums you ticked. Free up space is a cleaning tool for the phone as a whole \u2014 duplicates and your largest files are found in every album, ticked or not, because a duplicate wastes space wherever it sits. If Files looks empty, the usual reason is that no album is ticked yet; the list says so, and Settings has the album picker.
Why is nothing happening, or why did it stop?

Ente Saver works in the background and waits for good moments on purpose, so a quiet hour is normal. When it waits longer, one of these is the reason, and Home says which. Battery Saver pauses it until Battery Saver is off (most phones switch it off while charging); Super power saving or Ultra battery saver stops every background app while it is on. Charging-only mode waits for the charger. On Realme, Oppo, Xiaomi and Vivo phones, auto-launch switched off is the usual reason it stops a day after setup \u2014 Settings \u203a Permissions and battery opens that page, with the path to it. Android also runs an app less often when it is rarely opened; opening Ente Saver now and then helps. Optimise now on Home runs it straight away, within the safety limits.
How do I know this copy of Ente Saver is the real one?

Every official build is published at github.com/smmpanelusertestai07-dotcom/EnteSaver, and each release prints two long codes: one for the file itself and one for the key it was signed with. The file\u2019s code changes with every build; the key\u2019s code is the same for every genuine Ente Saver there will ever be. Android checks that key for you: a build signed with a different one cannot install over this app at all. Installed on its own, after this one is removed, it would open and say so on Home, and it would keep deletion switched off. Installing from a file rather than a store is also why the phone shows a Play Protect warning the first time: \u201cMore details\u201d, then \u201cInstall anyway\u201d.

Ente Saver has no internet permission, so it cannot send anything anywhere. There is no account to create and no sign-in. There are no ads and no analytics of any kind. It also keeps its records out of Android\u2019s own backup and phone-to-phone transfer, so the system never copies them anywhere. A reinstall or a new phone is set up from the app\u2019s history file instead, when you choose to restore it.

It reads your gallery\u2019s index for every album \u2014 names, sizes and dates \u2014 so it can count and list them. Only the albums you tick are optimised or copied. Albums you leave out are counted, never changed. You can change the list at any time in Settings.

File names, dates, sizes and a short code that identifies each file \u2014 the details needed to avoid doing the same work twice. Never your photos, and never thumbnails of them. It is all kept on the phone. A copy of this list is saved daily as history.json in Documents \u203a Ente Saver. A reinstall or a new phone can pick up from it.

It never edits, moves or deletes your originals on its own. The only removals of originals come from you, through Android\'s own confirmation. Its own copies are cleared to stay within the space you allow, best-proven and oldest first. No original is ever removed to make room.

No Android app can be made impossible to inspect, and anyone claiming otherwise is selling something. Ente Saver protects you by holding no secrets worth stealing and by checking that its own code has not been altered.
The app is provided as is, without warranty of any kind. It is a helper, not a backup service. Keep checking Ente Photos yourself.

resources.string: Your file history already saves itself once a day, as history.json in Documents \u203a Ente Saver. After a reinstall or on a new phone, choose that file with Restore. The buttons below are only for an extra copy you keep somewhere else.
Ente Saver checks from the outside — it can never look inside %1$s. Before you continue, open %1$s and check a few of these files are really there.
Ente Saver checks from the outside — it can never look inside Ente Photos. Before you continue, open it and check a few of these files are really there.
Light copies stay on this phone

These live in your gallery like any other photo. Ente Saver never optimises them again, never uploads them, and never removes one on its own. One thing to avoid: do not add the Light copies album to Ente\'s backed up folders — every file here already reached Ente once, and backing the album up would store it twice.
Keep this album out of Ente\'s backed up folders — these files are already in Ente.
Every place a file can disappear from, and what actually happens next. In every row, your originals are only ever removed by you.
An optimised copy in the Ente Saver folder

If it was already confirmed as backed up, nothing happens — a disappearing copy is exactly what an upload looks like. If it was not yet confirmed, Ente Saver remakes the copy from your original and puts it back in the upload folder. If the same copy keeps vanishing before it is collected, the file is set aside and listed under Skipped instead of looping.
An original photo or video in your gallery

Ente Saver never deletes an original by itself, so this only happens by your hand or another app\'s. Anything already in Ente stays there. If the file had not been optimised yet, there is simply nothing left to optimise, and the app stops counting it.
A kept light copy in Pictures/Light copies
That album belongs to you and Ente Saver never touches it. Removing a light copy only frees phone space — the file is still in Ente, and nothing is optimised or sent again.
The history file in Documents \u203a Ente Saver

Written again within a day, automatically, with no chip and no alert. The history is only lost if the file is deleted and the app is reinstalled before the next daily save \u2014 and even then your photos and your Ente account are unaffected.

Ente Saver cannot see inside Ente, so it does not notice — and it will not send the file again, because its record says the file was already delivered. Restore it from Ente\'s own trash. This is why the free-up screen asks you to open Ente Photos and look before removing originals.
Ente Saver itself — uninstalled, or its data cleared

Nothing happens to your files: originals stay, copies stay in the Ente Saver folder until Ente Photos collects them, kept light copies stay, and your Ente account is untouched. Keep the app\u2019s data when Android asks, or choose history.json in Documents \u203a Ente Saver with Restore on the first screen, and it carries on where it stopped.
Something was deleted — what happens now?

Only if you used Ente Saver before, on this phone or an old one. Choose history.json in Documents \u203a Ente Saver, or a backup you saved. It brings back your settings and the record of what already reached Ente, so nothing is optimised or sent twice. It never touches your photos. New here? Skip it and tap Get started.
Ente Saver can only see the photos you picked, so the trial cannot run. Choose \"Allow all\" in app permissions to use it.
Tick at least one album first \u2014 the trial uses the albums you chose.

Optimises up to 3 photos from the albums you chose, so you can see the size and quality before anything else happens. The copies stay inside the app until you start, and your originals are never touched.
Try it on a few photos
